priorInvolvementDisclosure: I returned ACCEPT on v2 at 0/0/0 and Codex returned REJECT with two SHOULD-FIX findings, both real. That makes every ACCEPT I have issued across these two lineages wrong, five for five, while every REJECT has been corroborated. I have named a different single cause each time and been wrong again on the next ACCEPT, so the honest reading is not that I have finally found the flaw in my method. The pattern is that I test thoroughly in the dimension that failed last time and miss an adjacent one. At v2 specifically I quoted the phrase 'including component-originated CA-4 egress' as evidence the repair was phase-exact, when that phrase is the mistyping Codex found, because I never looked up what CA-4 is defined to mean in the artifacts the candidate cites. The operative consequence is about weight: my finding nothing is weak evidence that there is nothing, and I say so in the verdict rather than issuing a clean bill. Three tests drawn from actual misses were run this round for the first time: byte-searching for concepts the cited inputs contain that the candidate never mentions, which is how Codex found PT-NET-EGRESS absent from v2; testing every closure word against the artifact's own carried sources rather than its siblings, which is what 'exactly' failed at v2; and looking up every type name against its definition in the cited artifacts. The finding below came from the fourth: applying the completeness-of-enumeration test to an enumeration I had never tested. I note that I am rejecting this round, so none of this is a hedge; the calibration statement stands on its own and applies to my ACCEPTs, not to this verdict.

shouldFix.title: The newly named inherited permission-recital conflict is declared unresolved in two places but is absent from remainingNamedNotResolved, the artifact's single enumeration of what remains unmet
evidence: The artifact declares the item unresolved twice. The new clause reads 'Permission-truth-tables v2/v6 recitals that treat CA-1/CA-2 together as producing an admitted-component PT-NET-EGRESS tail are an inherited conflict. This candidate names that conflict and does not silently resolve it.' The new fixture class reads 'FC-JOIN-INHERITED-PERM-RECITAL — permission v2/v6 CA-1/CA-2 PT-NET-EGRESS recital is named as an inherited conflict and is not silently resolved.'

remainingNamedNotResolved carries exactly the standing that describes: 'NAMED. Not resolved by this artifact.' Its five items are the FC-C1 joint-owner recording, DR-G09 and DR-114 fixture execution, BLK-1 through BLK-4, D-096 (A), and doctor v4's ID-DEP-12. The conflict is not among them.
I searched the item list for every plausible wording and found none: permission, recital, PT-NET-EGRESS, inherited, v2/v6 and conflict all return absent.
The list was not touched when the new unresolved item was introduced. v2 carried five items and v3 carries the same five, while v3 adds two extracted clauses and three fixture classes.

The obvious counter-reading, that the list is scoped to this contract's own leftovers rather than to unresolved matter inside other recorded artifacts, is defeated by the list's own fifth item. 'Doctor v4 ID-DEP-12 remains NAMED, NOT RESOLVED in doctor v4's own frozen bytes' is an unresolved item inside another recorded artifact's bytes. If that belongs on the list, an unresolved recital inside permission v2/v6's bytes belongs on it too, and the two are the same shape: a recorded artifact whose frozen text conflicts with the adopted position this candidate integrates.

The conflict is real rather than nominal, which is why its accounting matters. I verified the recital verbatim in both permission generations at /permissionVocabulary/tokens/[4].sliceJustification: 'This token covers COMPONENT-ORIGINATED egress only (a process doctor spawned under CA-1/CA-2, or any other admitted component).' Host-effect v25's ES-2b states the contrary for CA-2, that a customer tool's sockets are neither component PT-NET-EGRESS nor host CA-4. Two recorded artifacts disagree and this candidate is the one naming it.

This is the third instance of one defect class in three generations. DAJ1-CX-01 was a member missing from one enumeration while present in a sibling; DAJ2-CX-01 was an enumeration incomplete against the source the artifact itself carried; this is an enumeration not extended when the artifact added a member of exactly its declared category.
shouldFix.impact: remainingNamedNotResolved is the artifact's only roll-up of outstanding work and the place a coordinator or a successor author looks to see what this candidate leaves open. An unresolved conflict between two recorded artifacts, which this candidate is the first to name, does not appear there, so it can be dropped at the next generation without any enumeration showing a gap. That is the same mechanism by which the actor matrix lost CA-2 at v1 and the host roster lost the BLK-6 families at v2: the artifact stated the right thing in one place and did not carry it into the list that is supposed to be complete.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add a sixth item to remainingNamedNotResolved naming the inherited permission-truth-tables v2/v6 CA-1/CA-2 PT-NET-EGRESS recital conflict as named and not resolved by this artifact, in the same form as the existing doctor v4 ID-DEP-12 item. Do not resolve the conflict here; naming it in the roll-up is what the artifact already claims to do in the clause and the fixture class.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. Both of Codex's v2 findings are genuinely repaired and I verified each by execution: the closure claim is scoped to consentable CA-1..CA-4 attempts with the BLK-6 families carried separately, and the tail matrix is typed against the definitions in the artifacts the candidate cites, which is the check whose absence caused me to endorse the mistyped phrase at v2. I ran three tests for the first time this round, each drawn from an actual miss rather than invented, and all three came back clean. The finding came from a fourth: applying the completeness-of-enumeration test to remainingNamedNotResolved, which I had never tested. The artifact declares the inherited permission v2/v6 recital conflict named and not resolved in two places, that list carries exactly the standing 'NAMED. Not resolved by this artifact', and the conflict appears in none of its five items under any wording, while the list itself was left at five when the new item was introduced. The counter-reading that the list covers only this contract's own leftovers is defeated by its fifth item, which is an unresolved matter inside doctor v4's frozen bytes. I confirmed the conflict is real by finding the recital verbatim in both permission generations, and I resolved a false positive of my own before reporting anything. This is the third instance in three generations of one defect class, the artifact stating the right thing in one place and not carrying it into the list that is meant to be complete, and it is bounded to SHOULD-FIX for the same reason Codex bounded the first two: nothing is applied and nothing is hidden.
